data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A test constrains its subject rather than describes it whenever the test is the sole installation authority for the subject, because the test then cannot distinguish a subject that is wrong from a subject that the installation ritual has not yet authorized to be right.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the test can be run without installing the subject as an authority (e.g., in a sandbox where the subject is imported but not registered), and the same 3-of-26 distribution appears, the authority mechanism fails.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the 1-of-9 compile.py survivor is killed when the compile authority is refreshed before each mutation, then its survival is an authority-staleness artifact.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the 4/4-to-6/7 module gradient maps exactly to a known static property of each module (e.g., import order) rather than to installation order, the mechanism is incomplete.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If a second authority order produces the same survivor identities, the constraint is not authority-order-dependent.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The install-first authority pattern makes the test's pass/fail verdict a side effect of authorization rather than a measurement of the subject. In the 3-of-26 case, the first shown-to-fail mutation becomes the unauthorized baseline, and all later mutations are constrained by the registry's refusal to authorize a second failure. The compile.py 1-of-9 survivor is the one mutation whose failure path was not reachable under the installed authority, so it was never constrained; the 4/4-to-6/7 modules are those whose authority path was partially blocked by the first failure, producing a gradient of constraint rather than a binary description.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
